[[Rosenberg, Texas|Rosenberg]], Texas }} '''Dexter Jerome Pittman''' (born March 2, 1988 in [[Rosenberg, Texas]]) is a [[college basketball]] player for the [[University of Texas at Austin]]. Pittman left the NBA draft combine to be with his family following the death of his fifteen year old brother who was shot in Houston on May 5th 2010. ==High school== Pittman was a 3 year starter at [[B. F. Terry High School]], where he averaged 15 points and 8.5 rebounds per game over his career. In his senior season, he was named the Most Valuable Player for District 24-4A.{{cite news | url=http://www.texassports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/pittman_dexter00.html | title=Dexter Pittman | work=TexasSports | publisher=[[The University of Texas]] | accessdate=2009-06-27}} He verbally committed to the [[University of Texas]] in October 2005, over scholarship offers from [[Texas A&M University|Texas A&M]] and [[Arizona State]].{{cite news | url=http://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/viewprospect.asp?pr_key=32759&Sport=2 | title=Dexter Pittman Profile - Basketball Recruiting | publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] | accessdate=2009-06-27}} He was ranked as the 16th best center prospect out of high school, as well as one of the top 150 high school players in the nation. ==College== Pittman was used sparingly in his first two seasons at Texas, averaging less than 3 points per game with just one start. As a junior, he started 24 games, averaging 10 points and 5.5 rebounds per game{{cite news | url=http://www.texassports.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/2008-2009/texasmbbstats.html | title=2009 Season Statistics | work=TexasSports | publisher=[[The University of Texas]] | accessdate=2009-06-27}}, and became one of the most dominant centers in the [[Big 12 conference]].{{cite news | url=http://www.big12sports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?PRINTABLE_PAGE=YES&ATCLID=3672855 | title=Texas Student-Athlete Spotlight: Dexter Pittman | publisher=[[Big 12 Conference]] | author=Dan Hurwitz| accessdate=2009-06-27}} ===Weight Loss=== Pittman weighed 388 lbs as a senior at [[B. F. Terry High School|Terry High School]]. After receiving weight loss tips from Texas' Strength and Conditioning coach [[Todd Wright]], he was able to drop his weight to 366 lbs before enrolling at Texas. His weight still prevented him from doing basic drills in practice, which caused various back and knee aches. Pittman then dedicated himself to a workout program with Wright, which included 5:30 AM workouts and a complete revamp of his diet. Pittman agreed to call [[Todd Wright]] before every meal to evaluate his choices. He later characterized the workout regimen as so tough that "I wanted to cry and say, 'Man, I want to give up'". Since losing almost 100 pounds, he has become an icon for admirers, like [[Basketball Hall of Fame|Hall of Famer]] [[Charles Barkley]]{{cite news | url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sharedcontent/dws/spt/colleges/national/tournament/ncaamen/stories/031909dnspocarltonut.34feb9c.html | title=Pittman's role is now what's huge at Texas | publisher=[[Dallas Morning News]] | author=Chuck Carlton | accessdate=2009-06-27}}, who heard about his weight loss. ==References== {{reflist}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Pittman, Dexter}} [[Category:1988 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Texas]] [[Category:Texas Longhorns men's basketball players]]
